<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a dominant M peak at 121, an M+1 peak at ~8 % intensity, and rapidly decreasing higher‑mass peaks—the pattern matches the natural ^13C distribution for a molecule containing several carbons. No characteristic 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) M+2 intensities are present, and the M+2 intensity is far too low for sulfur. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the spectrum.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
